prompt: In duration.js export (CommonJS, module.exports = { parseDuration }) a function parseDuration(text) that returns a whole number of milliseconds. If text is not a string throw TypeError. Leading and trailing whitespace is ignored; after trimming the text must be one or more components written back to back with no whitespace between them, each component being a number followed by a unit. A number is digits with an optional fractional part ('1', '1.5'; a leading '.', a trailing '.' and signs are invalid). The units are h, m, s and ms. Units must appear in strictly decreasing order of size (h, then m, then s, then ms) and each unit may appear at most once. The result is the sum of number times the unit's milliseconds, rounded once with Math.round at the end. Anything else (empty text, an unknown unit, text that is not entirely components, a repeated or out-of-order unit) throws RangeError.
